name: Question 11
worked_solution:
First, recall the following:

- ${J}_{1}(-7)$ represents a $1\times 1$ Jordan block with $-7$'s on the leading diagonal,

- ${J}_{2}(-2)$ represents a $2\times 2$ Jordan block with $-2$'s on the leading diagonal.

Therefore, our Jordan blocks are given by

$$
{J}_{1}(-7)=[\begin{aligned}-7\end{aligned}],\,{J}_{2}(-2)=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

The composition of our Jordan blocks gives the following block diagonal matrix:

$$
{J}_{1}(-7)\,⊕\,{J}_{2}(-2)=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 11
?

J1(−7)⊕J2(−2)=

a
[−7000−2100−2]
b
[−7100−2100−2]
c
[−7100−7100−2]
d
[−7000−2000−2]
e
[−7000−7000−2]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, recall the following:

  • J1(−7) represents a 1×1 Jordan block with −7's on the leading diagonal,

  • J2(−2) represents a 2×2 Jordan block with −2's on the leading diagonal.

Therefore, our Jordan blocks are given by J1(−7)=[−7],J2(−2)=[−210−2].

The composition of our Jordan blocks gives the following block diagonal matrix:

J1(−7)⊕J2(−2)=[−7000−2100−2]
